# Implement cross-platform installer

## 任务摘要
- 类型: 开发实现（`develop`）
- 执行角色: 独立评审者（`reviewer`）
- 目标: Deliver the existing diagnosis and Compact/External Cluster installer, including Linux no-cluster K3s bootstrap from an OAC-authenticated embedded exact upstream pin catalog, and a fail-closed consumer of the signed system-release installation/resource/readiness index. The installer owner implements this within its current two source roots, with executable isolated fixtures and immutable source provenance; it does not wait for downstream release assembly to implement or test the consumer, and does not claim production installation or full-journey acceptance.

OWNERS AND INPUT BOUNDARY. Keep installer/codex-macmini-newapi as the sole implementation and source producer for cmd/oac-installer/install/** and internal/installer/**. Add the embedded K3s pin catalog, pinned upstream install.sh, production loader/verification and install adapters, resource/readiness decoder, and complete test-only signed fixtures below internal/installer; these are constituent sources of the existing installer component, not a new source owner or independent service. Freeze them in the same reviewed Git commit/tree/blobs and installer source bundle/component-manifest already consumed by installer-entrypoint -> installer-binary -> system-release-assembly. No future Installer implementation exists in the bound worker source c9e7663846f310ba919644d07583044f97a8983e. All new paths and test names below are required Worker deliverables, not claims that files already exist.

EXACT LINUX PAYLOAD. Select linux/amd64 K3s v1.34.12+k3s1, official release https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/releases/tag/v1.34.12%2Bk3s1 (release ID 400219926), source commit 47b4749964eb62628618bedad32eeacfc9eebbae. This minor aligns with the bound go.mod k8s.io/api, apimachinery and client-go v0.34.1; it is not proof of OAC runtime compatibility. Keep the release compatibility preflight mandatory. The embedded catalog must contain exact version, OS/architecture, upstream commit, HTTPS locators, byte sizes and SHA256 for: (1) k3s, asset ID 601313077, 78000290 bytes, ef1df26b26276c0f6d962391c94e12f9362d1f1e30ec7a7926e9ddb84b0d66ce; (2) k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst, asset ID 601313085, 194444183 bytes, c2c6571bee0e2cee5cc3e248aa0edc0343bcbfc0e512589630030b635be3d581; both at https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/releases/download/v1.34.12%2Bk3s1/<exact filename>; (3) install.sh from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3s-io/k3s/47b4749964eb62628618bedad32eeacfc9eebbae/install.sh, 36455 bytes, 40b487f0d8ef4f5d1bf422e7bb6228cc7789c40ecc66c5ab067d396bbee9816e. Retain official sha256sum-amd64.txt, asset ID 601313835, 359 bytes, 2529ab5abe30b2d2db1e2f8018a67e75eb443381145316469538092d9958fbfd, as source evidence. Planner downloaded and hashed all four complete files, matched API sizes/digests and both payload entries in the checksum file, and executed none. Pin these bytes, not latest, a channel response, a floating tag resolution or get.k3s.io. Do not commit the large executable/image payloads into the source bundle; the catalog commits to their exact bytes and an offline cache is allowed only after the same checks.

AUTHENTICITY, NOT AN UNSIGNED-CHECKSUM BYPASS. The inspected upstream release has no detached signature assets; do not label GitHub API metadata, TLS, checksums or a test signer as an upstream K3s signature. Use the existing OAC signing chain: installer owns the catalog and embedded exact script as reviewed source; installer-entrypoint links that source; installer-binary is the existing producing/signing owner of the complete compatible installer binary, whose signature therefore commits to the embedded catalog and script; system-release-assembly binds that installer and its signature inputs in the signed release. Before any privileged payload execution, an independently trusted OAC release/installer verifier must authenticate the exact executable and release against the configured OAC public-key/key-ID trust authority, then the installer verifies the catalog-selected binary and image bytes against their authenticated pins. This is OAC-signed digest binding of third-party payloads, not a claim of upstream detached signing. Accept the existing oac.installer-signatures/v1 envelope and openssl-dgst-sha256 semantics from the bound release tooling; do not introduce a new signature algorithm or trust service. Trust material cannot come from the untrusted payload being checked, from TOFU or from a download beside it. No bypass flag, test key or unsigned development binary is eligible for production bootstrap. Missing production signer/trust evidence blocks production release/use; local fixture verification does not manufacture it. Read-only public downloads and digest checks are permitted during implementation; root commands and live clusters are not.

INSTALL METHOD. After host/target, resource, privilege, kernel/cgroup, network, storage and ingress preflight and explicit user confirmation of the exact local target, stage only verified bytes in a private directory without traversal/symlink/hardlink escapes. Recheck immediately before use, atomically place the executable at /usr/local/bin/k3s and the exact image archive at /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images/k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst, and invoke the embedded verified script through the host shell with explicit argv 'server --write-kubeconfig-mode=600', INSTALL_K3S_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=true and INSTALL_K3S_SKIP_SELINUX_RPM=true in an allowlisted environment. No pipe-to-shell, channel lookup, mutable script download, uncontrolled inherited K3S_URL/K3S_TOKEN/INSTALL_K3S_* variables, optional RPM download, firewall disabling, SELinux disabling or automatic infrastructure upgrade is permitted. Preflight must reject a SELinux host without already compatible policy and name the repair; never set INSTALL_K3S_SELINUX_WARN=true. Keep local-path and Traefik defaults. The native installer release already targets linux-amd64; other OS/architecture paths must not execute this payload. macOS/Windows still reuse compatible selected Kubernetes or stop with guidance. Existing Kubernetes/K3s is reused only when explicitly selected and compatible, never overwritten/upgraded by this bootstrap. Observe exact owned files/service, cluster identity and installation identity before retry after lost responses; unknown/stale/contradictory observations block a second side effect. Protect kubeconfig and bootstrap material, do not collect an administrator password, and never reopen an already consumed first-admin bootstrap.

PRODUCTION RESOURCE/READINESS INPUT. The immutable producing owner remains system-release-assembly, not installer or Software Delivery release-preview. Its current contract already requires packaging/system-release/schemas/system-release-manifest.schema.json, packaging/system-release/schemas/system-release-installation-index.schema.json and artifacts/system-release-assembly/installation-index.json, complete-release-n-plus-1.tar.zst, component/input indexes, payload locators and release signature. platform-workload-manifest-bundle owns fixed Kubernetes resources and Artifact Storage; platform-schema-migration-bundle owns CRD/OpenAPI and replayable migrations; installer-binary owns signed installer executables. Those producers are unchanged. Consume their release as a runtime installation argument, not an upstream build input or a new blocked_by edge: assembly already transitively depends on installer and the reverse edge would be cyclic. The 17-line bound schemas/system-release-manifest.schema.json is a historical tooling fixture schema, not proof of a complete production installation index; do not mutate it or accept its opaque artifact alone as complete production input.

The installer must decode the assembly-owned typed index into one bounded internal installation input model, not publish a second production index/schema. Its accepted wire contract must bind the exact system SemVer/artifact digest, installer compatibility, Kubernetes compatibility and selected deployment mode; each indexed member must have a safe bundle-relative path, SHA256/size, producer/component identity and exact membership in the authenticated component/input indexes. Each Kubernetes resource must bind apiVersion/kind/namespace/name and its resource-document digest; each required readiness rule must bind that exact resource identity plus a typed probe/condition and fresh observation requirements. Resolve namespace/storage/ingress defaults and user-selected overrides into one deterministic installation identity, with pre-mutation reconfirmation if the target changes. Reject missing/extra/duplicate members, duplicate resource identities, unsafe paths, unknown required schema/probe kinds, mutable image references, unbound OCI config/descriptor digests, compatibility unknown, and an index or readiness rule not transitively authenticated by the release signature and artifact bytes. Verify the complete signed envelope and closure before any host/cluster mutation; signature success over an opaque blob is insufficient. The system-release-assembly producer remains responsible for its public schema and byte serialization; internal Go decoding and consumer fixtures do not take that ownership. Test the consumer against complete representative signed assembly envelopes under internal/installer/testdata, marking every such envelope fixture-only and never treating it as a production release. A future producer/consumer wire mismatch must fail its existing assembly/integration gates, not cause a permissive fallback or a live contract edit.

Required resource closure is the owning deploy-ops sections 2/3: exactly the four fixed Deployments and Services, Workflow CRD, Compact PostgreSQL StatefulSet/Service/PVC or exact External PostgreSQL binding, Artifact Storage with Compact persistent/minimal implementation or External endpoint plus credential reference, ServiceAccounts and least-privilege RBAC/Bindings, Lease permissions when applicable, ConfigMaps/Secret references, NetworkPolicy/PDB/monitoring, ingress or Gateway, and the replayable compatible schema/migration set. No shadow AgentRun/WorkUnit CRD. Readiness must prove Kubernetes API and Node Ready after K3s, then CRD Established and required RBAC, migrations complete, bound PVC/storage connectivity, PostgreSQL and Artifact Storage compatibility/connectivity/readiness, all four Deployments with current observedGeneration and available replicas, selected Service/ingress reachability and the same Web/API endpoint. Installer reads Kubernetes/deployment probes directly, never QueryPlatformOperations or the Orchestrator Kernel; missing/stale/timeout/conflicting required facts remain unknown, never green. Do not print/open the Web URL as installation success until all required observations pass. Full three-OS browser/live installation evidence remains int-platform-release and final-acceptance-closeout, with external environment authority expressly DEFERRED.

LOCAL VERIFICATION BOUNDARY. Implement all new tests in internal/installer (same Go package tree) using real cryptographic fixture signatures, isolated filesystem/process/network/Kubernetes adapters, controlled clocks and complete signed resource indexes. Positive fixture runs may execute only test helper processes in temporary directories, never upstream install.sh or k3s, service managers, privileged filesystem writes or a real cluster. Public upstream-byte verification is a separate read-only catalog check; do not substitute tiny fixture bytes for the exact upstream hashes. Test-signing keys are generated in test temporary directories and cannot become production trust roots. Preserve 90% coverage across cmd/oac-installer/install/... and internal/installer/..., source ownership closure and all current acceptance responsibilities. Fixtures prove implementation behavior only; they do not assert real readiness or grant external execution authority.

## 任务详情
Smallest independently PR-able, testable and reviewable delivery boundary for this capability.

## 非目标
- Do not change adjacent domain ownership or introduce a competing source of truth.
- Do not bypass authorization, admission, CAS, idempotency, review or evidence gates.
- Do not preserve unpublished prototype behavior unless the owning design explicitly requires it.
- Do not rewrite the historical Installer v2 owner-decision, source/failure/review history, absolute counters, retained approved budgets, completed nodes or another owner contract. No acceptance responsibility migration, source-owner transfer, new dependency or typed IO policy is part of this change; the existing omitted consumes remains omitted.
- Do not edit the shared release-tooling schema or pretend its opaque fixture artifact is a complete installation input. Do not re-own production release assembly, fixed workloads, migrations, signed installer packaging, root entrypoint, upgrade/rollback or full-flow acceptance.
- Do not introduce live or privileged verification, claim Linux pre-provisioning satisfies the no-cluster journey, or ask the human to select routine internal versions/ownership. External clusters/namespaces/resources/fault injection remain DEFERRED.
- Do not use unsigned checksums as signatures, invent upstream signatures or production keys, permit test trust on a production path, weaken Required readiness/compatibility, silently switch context, or retry an unknown side effect.

- `cmd/oac-installer/install/**`
